items.title: Qwen3-Coder template: model fails to trigger XML tool calls with large prompts — request JSON format option
items.body:
[llama_cpp_issue.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30672460/llama_cpp_issue.md)
**Title: Qwen3-Coder template: model often fails to trigger XML tool calls with large prompts — request JSON format option**

## Summary

Qwen3-Coder models (Qwen3.5/Qwen3.6 based) using the built-in specialized template often **fail to output `<tool_call>`** when presented with large system prompts and many tools (e.g., 20+ tools, 10K+ token prompts typically sent by AI agent frameworks). The model responds with plain text instead of making tool calls, even though the lazy PEG-native grammar is correctly generated and waiting.

The issue became visible after PR #24869 (AC parser, merged Jun 21 2026) improved XML grammar generation. Older builds (b8646, Apr 3 2026) accidentally worked around this because the old delimiter parser would fail on complex multi-tool grammars and fall back to a JSON array grammar — the JSON tool instructions were more reliably followed by the model.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start llama-server with a Qwen3.5-based GGUF model:
   ```
   llama-server -m Qwen3.5-model.gguf --reasoning off --jinja --port 1234
   ```
2. Send a `/v1/chat/completions` request with 20+ tool definitions and a long system prompt (10K+ tokens total), `tool_choice: "auto"` (default)
3. The model responds with plain text content (e.g., "I'll help you create...") with `finish_reason: "stop"` instead of `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`

The lazy grammar is correctly generated but **never triggered** — `Grammar still awaiting trigger after token ... (<|im_end|>)`.

For comparison, the identical request with `tool_choice: "required"` works correctly.

## Root Cause

The Qwen3-Coder template injects XML-format tool instructions (`<function=name>`, `<parameter=x>`) into the system prompt. The model, when faced with large/complex prompts, tends to output text instead of voluntarily initiating the XML tool call format.

The old parser (pre-#24869) had a bug where complex XML grammars with many tools would fail to parse:
```
parse: error parsing grammar: number of rules that are going to be repeated multiplied by the new repetition exceeds sa...
```
This failure caused a fallback to JSON array grammar format, whose corresponding tool instructions happened to be better followed by the model.

## Proposed Solution

Add support for a `tool_call_format` option in the Qwen3-Coder specialized template (controllable via `--chat-template-kwargs`), allowing users to choose `"json"` format for tool calls instead of the default XML. For example:

```
--chat-template-kwargs '{"tool_call_format": "json"}'
```

This would:
1. Generate JSON-format tool instructions in the system prompt
2. Use the JSON array grammar (like the old accidental fallback)
3. Improve tool call reliability for Qwen3-Coder models in agent scenarios

## Environment

- llama.cpp build b10237 (2b63e0610)
- Model: Qwen3.5-9B based (CoPaw-Flash-9B-Q4_K_M, `qwen35` architecture)
- ROCm backend, AMD Radeon 8060S
- Windows 11

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4-Flash on sm_121 (GB10): deterministic character-level output corruption — quant/build-independent
items.body:
## Description

Serving a DeepSeek-V4-Flash GGUF on GB10 (sm_121) produces **deterministic, character-level output corruption** when the model reproduces text from its own context. It is 100% reproducible at temperature 0, survives two llama.cpp builds, two different quantizations (MXFP4 and Q2_K_S), and is absent when the same model runs hosted. Output is fluent and plausible — the defect only becomes visible when the model must reproduce exact character sequences (agent workloads: tool calls, paths, shell commands).

Typical failure: asked to echo the exact string

```
ls -la ~/.ssh/config 2>/dev/null | head -20 && hostname && whoami
```

temp 0 returns (deterministic across 5/5 reps):

```
ls -la ~/.ssh/config 2>/dev/nll | head -20 && hostname && whoam
```

The model also *misreads its own prompt*: in reasoning_content it restates the canary dozens of times, each time with different mutations (`2>dev/null`, `2/dev/null`, `2>>/dev/null`, `hosname`, `whoam`, `head 20`), blames the "user's typos", re-reads to resolve the contradiction, produces a new mutation, and spirals until the token budget exhausts (empty content, `finish_reason: length`). This is the generator of agent-facing loop/corruption failures.

## Steps to reproduce

Single request against the server (any of the 4 configs below):

```bash
curl http://<host>:8081/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model": "deepseek-v4-flash",
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Repeat the following shell command back to me EXACTLY, character for character, on a single line, with nothing before or after it and no code fence:\nls -la ~/.ssh/config 2>/dev/null | head -20 && hostname && whoami"}],
  "temperature": 0,
  "max_tokens": 3000,
  "stream": false
}'
```

Expected: the canary echoed byte-exact. Observed: never byte-exact (0/10 echo + 0/5 tool-call args across every configuration below).

## Exoneration matrix (same 65-char canary, temp 0, n≥5 per arm)

| Variable | Result |
|---|---|
| MTP on / off (`--model-draft`, `--spec-draft-n-max 2`) | corrupts either way |
| `--reasoning-budget 1024` on / off | corrupts either way (budget only moves the spiral from empty-content to content-overflow) |
| temperature 0.0 / 1.0 | corrupts either way; temp 0 is fully deterministic |
| llama.cpp `4df29be4f` (b10454) and `85c55223c` (b10726) | corrupts on both |
| **Quant: MXFP4 GGUF AND Q2_K_S GGUF of the same model** | **corrupts identically on both → the GGUF files and the MXFP4 matmul are not the cause** |
| Samplers | repeat-penalty 1.1 + DRY deployed; failure predates and survives them |
| Tokenizer / template | `/tokenize`→`/detokenize` round-trip byte-exact; `/apply-template` renders the prompt byte-perfect → the corruption is in the forward pass |

**Discriminators:**

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| Hosted `deepseek-v4-flash` (official DeepSeek API, same prompt) | **10/10 byte-exact**, 86–697 chars reasoning, ~1.1 s/request |
| `gpt-oss-20b` **MXFP4** GGUF, single node, same binary, same sm_121 hardware | **15/15 byte-exact** (echo 10/10, tool args 5/5) → generic MXFP4 MMQ kernels are fine |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash locally (all configs, 40 requests) | 0 byte-exact |

So: model weights fine (hosted), generic MXFP4 kernels fine (gpt-oss), quant file fine (Q2_K_S also corrupts). What remains specific to this deployment: **the DeepSeek-V4 architecture-specific paths (DSA sparse-attention indexer, MLA, MoE routing) executed on sm_121**, and the 2-node RPC tensor split (could not isolate: loading the full model on one node wedges the GB10 kernel during load — possibly a separate UVM issue).

## Related reports

- MLX #3879: "mxfp4 forward numerically wrong on Blackwell (sm_120/121)… individual ops fine, composed forward diverges ~25%… over 78 layers this compounds into degenerate logits" — same signature on the same silicon in a different runtime.
- llama.cpp #21371: custom CUDA quant kernels producing gibberish on Blackwell (fix: force cuBLAS) — same corruption class.

## Environment

- Hardware: 2× ASUS GX10 (NVIDIA GB10, sm_121, 121 GiB unified each), 200GbE DAC fabric, llama.cpp RPC tensor split 40/60
- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, kernel 6.17.0-1031-nvidia, aarch64, GCC 13.3.0
- Driver: 580.173.02 (CUDA 13.0); built with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER=/usr/local/cuda-13.0/bin/nvcc` (`/usr/local/cuda` symlinks to 13.3 — PTX-JIT builds are rejected by the 13.0 driver, so sm_121 SASS-native builds only)
- Build flags: `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121 -DGGML_CUDA=ON -DGGML_CUDA_FA=ON -DGGML_CUDA_FA_ALL_QUANTS=OFF -DGGML_RPC=ON -DGGML_RPC_RDMA=ON -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON` (Release)
- Server flags: `-m DeepSeek-V4-Flash-{MXFP4,Q2_K_S}-00001-of-00002.gguf --model-draft mtp-...gguf --spec-draft-n-max 2 --rpc 10.0.0.2:50052 -ngl 99 --tensor-split 40,60 --repeat-penalty 1.1 --dry-multiplier 0.4 --dry-allowed-length 3 --dry-penalty-last-n 256 --reasoning-budget 1024 --alias deepseek-v4-flash --port 8081`

## Ask

Help isolating which sm_121 kernel path (DSA indexer / MLA / MoE for the DeepSeek-V4 architecture) could emit subtly wrong hidden states for context tokens — e.g. a flag to force dequant/cuBLAS/CPU for those paths, or a pointer to known sm_121 numerics issues in those kernels. Full probe harness and logs available on request.

items.title: Misc. bug: json-schema-to-grammar — nested string maxLength >= 2000 emits un-parseable GBNF (tool-call grammar, b10034)
items.body:
### Name and Version

version: **b10034 (505b1ed15)**, CUDA build, `llama-server` in router mode.

```
$ curl -s localhost:8000/props | jq .build_info
"b10034-505b1ed15"
```

### Operating systems

Linux

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server (`--jinja` tool-call grammar / json-schema-to-grammar)

### Command line

```shell
llama-server --jinja --model Qwen3.6-35BA3B-MTP-Q4_0.gguf \
  --ctx-size 262144 --n-gpu-layers 100 --flash-attn on --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

A tool whose JSON-Schema has a **string with `maxLength >= 2000` nested inside a sub-object** makes the `--jinja` tool-call grammar generator emit GBNF that fails its own parser:

```
400 Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar
```

The repetition cap that prevents this for **top-level** string properties (added in #23902 / discussed in #20867, `MAX_REPETITION_THRESHOLD = 2000`) is **not applied when the string is one object deeper**. As a result any request carrying such a tool is rejected with HTTP 400 and no tool call can be made.

This surfaced with a real agent framework (OpenClaw 2026.7.x) whose `cron` tool has `patch.trigger.anyOf[].script` = `{ "type": "string", "maxLength": 65536 }`. Every tool-using turn on the model 400s.

**Minimal repro — FAILS (400):** string `maxLength=2000` nested one object deep

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"any","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}],"tool_choice":"auto",
  "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"t","description":"d","parameters":{
    "type":"object","properties":{
      "o":{"type":"object","properties":{
        "s":{"type":"string","maxLength":2000}}}}}}}]}'
# -> 400 Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar
```

**Passes (200):** identical but `maxLength` at the **top level** (even 65536)

```bash
... "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"s":{"type":"string","maxLength":65536}}} ...   # 200
```

**Threshold matches MAX_REPETITION_THRESHOLD:**

| placement | maxLength | result |
|---|---|---|
| top-level | 65536 | 200 |
| nested (1 object deep) | 1000 | 200 |
| nested (1 object deep) | 2000 | **400 failed to parse grammar** |
| nested (1 object deep) | 65536 | **400 failed to parse grammar** |

Removing `maxLength` (or capping it < 2000) makes the nested case pass. The fix is presumably to apply the same repetition cap in the nested-object schema path that already protects top-level properties.

### Related

- #20867 `MAX_REPETITION_THRESHOLD (2000)` breaks tool-calling grammars — same threshold, but that/#23902 only cap top-level; nested objects still overflow on b10034.
- #24658 tool-call grammar generator emits GBNF that fails its own parser (open) — same symptom, different trigger.
- Separately, the same toolset also hits #22314 (closed/stale): an unanchored PCRE-shorthand `pattern` (`"\\S"`) yields `Unable to generate parser ... Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'`. Minimal repro: a tool string property with `"pattern": "\\S"`.

### First Bad Commit

Unknown (present in b10034).

### Relevant log output

```
srv  ... Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar
```

items.body:
# `tool_choice: "required"` is accepted but not enforced on templates with `supports_preserve_reasoning: true`

### Name and Version

```
build_info: b330-84e908c62
```
Built locally for CUDA 13.0, `-DGGML_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121 -DCMAKE_CUDA_FLAGS="-O2"`.

### Operating systems

Linux (aarch64, NVIDIA GB10 / sm_121)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

`llama-server`, and the chat/grammar layer under `common/` (`chat-auto-parser-generator.cpp`).

### Command line

```
llama-server -m qwen36-NVFP4-MTP-HQ.gguf --host 0.0.0.0 --port 11435 \
  -c 131072 --jinja -ngl 999 -fa on -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 --spec-type draft-mtp
```

### Problem description

`llama-server` accepts `"tool_choice": "required"` on `/v1/chat/completions` without error or
warning, and then does not enforce it, on models whose chat template llama.cpp classifies with
`supports_preserve_reasoning: true`.

Instead of being constrained to emit a tool call, the model generates freely until `max_tokens`
is exhausted. The request returns `finish_reason: "length"` with `predicted_n` equal to the full
budget and no `tool_calls`. In the runs I inspected the tail of the output had degenerated into a
repeating emoji sequence, which is consistent with generation being unconstrained rather than
grammar-limited.

The failure is **silent and expensive**: a caller that relies on `required` for structured output
receives ordinary prose, no error, and pays the maximum token cost of the request every time.

Two servers on the same host, same binary, same build string, both `--jinja`, differ only in the
model/template:

| | fast lane | smart lane |
|---|---|---|
| model | Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (NVFP4, MTP) | Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct (Q4_K_M) |
| `supports_tool_calls` | true | true |
| `supports_parallel_tool_calls` | true | true |
| `supports_object_arguments` | true | true |
| **`supports_preserve_reasoning`** | **true** | **false** |
| `tool_choice: "required"` | **ignored** | honoured |

`supports_preserve_reasoning` is the only differing capability in `/props → chat_template_caps`.

**On reproducing this without my exact file:** the GGUF above is a local conversion and is not
something you can download, so please do not treat the filename as the repro target. The trigger
appears to be the *chat template* — specifically whichever templates llama.cpp classifies
`supports_preserve_reasoning: true`, i.e. a `<think>`-style reasoning template. Any model whose
`/props → chat_template_caps` reports that flag together with `supports_tool_calls: true` should
show it. `repro.sh` prints both flags up front so it is obvious at a glance whether a given server
is a candidate. I am happy to attach the exact template text if that helps.

### What is NOT the cause (ruled out by measurement)

- **The model.** An identical hand-written GBNF grammar posted to `/completion` forces a perfect
  tool call on both servers, from a prompt with no intent to call anything. Section B of the
  reproducer is this control.
- **Grammar sampling generally.** `root ::= "BANANA"` is honoured on the affected server.
- **Speculative decoding.** The control above succeeds with `--spec-type draft-mtp` active.
- **Reasoning parsing.** Sending `"reasoning_format": "none"` does not change the behaviour.
- **Token budget.** Identical failure at `max_tokens` 500 / 1500 / 3000 / 5000 — all fully
  consumed, `reasoning_content` exactly 801 chars each time.
- **The tool-call syntax.** Both templates emit `<tool_call>…</tool_call>` with `<|im_start|>`.

### Why this looks like a defect rather than unsupported behaviour

`common/chat-auto-parser-generator.cpp` appears to intend enforcement on this path:

```cpp
// ~line 84
bool include_grammar = has_response_format || (has_tools &&
        ((inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_AUTO && !trigger_marker.empty()) ||
          inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_REQUIRED));

// ~line 89 — REQUIRED yields a NON-lazy (eager) grammar
data.grammar_lazy = !has_response_format && inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_AUTO;

// ~line 369 and ~line 500 — for REQUIRED the tool calls are NOT made optional
if (!require_calls) { tool_calls = p.optional(tool_calls); }
```

So a grammar is built, marked eager, and tool calls are non-optional — yet generation is
evidently unconstrained. I have not isolated the specific line where enforcement is lost; that
likely needs a debug build dumping the emitted GBNF for the two templates.

### Steps to Reproduce

Full script at the bottom of this issue. `./repro.sh <host:port>` exits **1** when the bug reproduces and **0**
when `required` is honoured — it was verified to discriminate between the two servers above.

```bash
curl -s http://HOST:PORT/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "model":"local",
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello, how are you today?"}],
  "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_disk_free",
    "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string"}},"required":["host"]}}}],
  "tool_choice":"required","max_tokens":2000,"temperature":0}'
```

Expected: a `tool_calls` response. Actual on an affected template: `finish_reason: "length"`,
`predicted_n` == `max_tokens`, no `tool_calls`.

### Relevant log output

```
finish_reason : length
predicted_n   : 2000
tool_calls    : NONE
content tail  : '🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️🎗️…'

# control, same server, hand-written grammar via /completion:
'<tool_call>{"name": "get_disk_free", "arguments": {"host": "beta"}}</tool_call>'
```


### Possibly related open issues

- **#26781** — *"enable_thinking forced true in jinja/caps.cpp capability probe leaks into
  non-DeepSeek templates"*. Same model family (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B), same subsystem, and a very
  similar end state: budget consumed inside `reasoning_content`, no `tool_calls`, a silent dead
  end for an API consumer. **Differences:** that report needs ~38-41 turns of accumulated context
  and ends `finish_reason: "stop"`; this one reproduces on a **single turn** and ends
  `finish_reason: "length"`, and it is specific to `tool_choice: "required"`, which that issue does
  not mention. Worth noting that my build **contains** the first-bad-commit bisected there
  (`0ef6e55e`, #26398 — verified with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`). If these share a root cause,
  the single-turn reproducer here may be the cheaper way to bisect it; happy to be closed as a
  duplicate if a maintainer sees them as the same defect.
- **#26530** — Qwen3-Coder template failing to emit `<tool_call>` with large prompts and many
  tools. Different trigger (prompt size, `auto` rather than `required`) but the same "template
  fails to produce a tool call" family.

### Separate, smaller issue found alongside

The OpenAI named-function form of `tool_choice` is rejected by type and silently downgraded to
the default on **both** servers:

```
W Wrong type supplied for parameter 'tool_choice'. Expected 'string',
  using default value: [json.exception.type_error.302] type must be string, but is object
```

`{"type":"function","function":{"name":"X"}}` is the documented OpenAI shape. Callers sending it
get `auto` behaviour with only a server-side log line. Worth either supporting the object form or
returning a 400 rather than silently changing the semantics of the request.


### `repro.sh`

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Minimal reproducer: tool_choice:"required" is accepted but not enforced
# on a chat template that llama.cpp classifies supports_preserve_reasoning=true.
#
# Usage: ./repro.sh <host:port>            e.g. ./repro.sh localhost:8080
# Exit 0 = required was honoured (no bug). Exit 1 = accepted-but-ignored (bug reproduced).
set -u
EP="${1:?usage: repro.sh <host:port>}"

TOOLS='[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"get_disk_free",
  "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string"}},"required":["host"]}}}]'
# A prompt the model has no reason to answer with a tool call. That is the point:
# tool_choice:"required" is supposed to compel one anyway.
MSG='[{"role":"user","content":"Hello, how are you today?"}]'

echo "== server =="
curl -s "http://$EP/props" | python3 -c "
import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin)
print('  model :', (d.get('model_path') or '?').split('/')[-1])
print('  build :', d.get('build_info'))
caps=d.get('chat_template_caps',{})
print('  supports_tool_calls        :', caps.get('supports_tool_calls'))
print('  supports_preserve_reasoning:', caps.get('supports_preserve_reasoning'))
"

echo
echo "== A. tool_choice:\"required\" (EXPECTED: a tool call) =="
RESP=$(curl -s "http://$EP/v1/chat/completions" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"model\":\"local\",\"messages\":$MSG,\"tools\":$TOOLS,\"tool_choice\":\"required\",\"max_tokens\":2000,\"temperature\":0}")
echo "$RESP" | python3 -c "
import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); c=d['choices'][0]; m=c['message']
tc=m.get('tool_calls')
print('  finish_reason :', c.get('finish_reason'))
print('  predicted_n   :', d.get('timings',{}).get('predicted_n'))
print('  tool_calls    :', tc[0]['function']['name'] if tc else 'NONE  <-- not enforced')
print('  content tail  :', repr((m.get('content') or '')[-80:]))
"
HAS_CALL=$(echo "$RESP" | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(1 if (json.load(sys.stdin)['choices'][0]['message'].get('tool_calls')) else 0)")

echo
echo "== B. CONTROL: same model, hand-written GBNF via /completion =="
echo "   (proves the model CAN be grammar-forced against its intent)"
curl -s "http://$EP/completion" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
 "prompt":"User asks: hello how are you?\nAssistant:",
 "grammar":"root ::= \"<tool_call>{\\\"name\\\": \\\"get_disk_free\\\", \\\"arguments\\\": {\\\"host\\\": \\\"\" host \"\\\"}}</tool_call>\"\nhost ::= \"alpha\" | \"beta\"",
 "n_predict":80,"temperature":0}' | python3 -c "
import json,sys; print('  output:', repr((json.load(sys.stdin).get('content') or '').strip())[:100])
"

echo
if [ "$HAS_CALL" = "1" ]; then
  echo "RESULT: required WAS honoured — bug not reproduced on this server."; exit 0
else
  echo "RESULT: BUG REPRODUCED — tool_choice:\"required\" accepted without error, no tool call,"
  echo "        full token budget consumed, while the control proves grammar forcing works."
  exit 1
fi
```

items.title: Eval bug: Malformed tokenizer metadata can cause ASan heap-buffer-overflow reads in vocab load
items.body:
### Name and Version

llama.cpp `master` at commit `7c082bc417bbe53210a83df4ba5b49e18ce6193c`.

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

CPU

### Hardware

Reproduced with CPU backend on Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9880H CPU @ 2.30GHz as exposed to a container.

### Models

```text
107e97d11dbaae3e89b5db2e98ec94b8a0bfc8404322fe6c48a07b46dd1b5d7d  scores-u8-oob.gguf
6d6be8fa0ad97a9854f1f6bb27e26e21a983e38fad31b16179d511919ca2d8e4  token-type-u8-oob.gguf
d0c0db44ab1835e1899ee650b258f26dbaf9fe0eb1bffe593f6768b83128a9bf  suppress-tokens-u8-oob.gguf
1a2ec352af9270e869400e5091918aa7c1a853e4930d871ab520d23b40e25ddd  ugm-short-charsmap-oob.gguf
```

These are minimized GGUF inputs, not Hugging Face models.

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

This is a follow-up to https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/24884 and https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/24885 from the same fuzzing run, but I am grouping the ASan heap-buffer-overflow reads here so they can be triaged in one place.

I also read `SECURITY.md`, which says that private security disclosure is disabled until further notice https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/security/policy.

With that in mind, there are two related validation problems here:

- narrow tokenizer metadata arrays are counted with `gguf_get_arr_n()` and then consumed as wider C++ element types without first validating `gguf_get_arr_type()`
- UGM `tokenizer.ggml.precompiled_charsmap` accepts a one-byte array, then reads the first four bytes as a `uint32_t` length before checking that four bytes are available

Expected behavior: reject malformed tokenizer metadata with normal load errors before reaching out-of-bounds reads.

Impact: any application that loads, validates, converts, indexes, or inspects user-provided GGUF files may trigger heap out-of-bounds reads during model/vocab loading. Under ASan these are deterministic crashes; without ASan the behavior is undefined. I have not attempted exploitability analysis beyond confirming the ASan OOB reads.

I am not going to submit any crashing samples or instructions publicly, but I can do so if that would help maintainers.


### First Bad Commit

Unknown. I have not bisected this.

### Relevant log output

I'm going to omit ASan traces here, but I can send them over if maintainers think it's useful.

items.title: Misc. bug: llama-server returns a tool-call id that its own chat template then rejects (Ministral-8B, --jinja)
items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 9632 (acd79d603)
built with AppleClang 21.0.0.21000101 for Darwin arm64
```

### Operating systems

Mac

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell
llama-server --model Ministral-8B-Instruct-2410-Q4_K_M.gguf --ctx-size 2048 \
             --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 --jinja
```

### Problem description

With `--jinja` and a Mistral model, **llama-server returns a tool-call `id` that it then rejects when that same `id` is echoed back**, which the OpenAI-compatible API requires the client to do. This makes a two-turn tool conversation impossible with this model.

Ministral-8B's bundled chat template validates the id format and raises:

```
Tool call IDs should be alphanumeric strings with length 9!
```

but the id llama-server hands back is `1697377797897` — 13 digits. The server does not reconcile the id it emits with the constraint the template it applies enforces.

The error surfaces as a 400 during *"Automatic parser generation"*, so it fails before the model is reached.

Model: `bartowski/Ministral-8B-Instruct-2410-GGUF`, `Ministral-8B-Instruct-2410-Q4_K_M.gguf`.

**Related but distinct: #11402.** Same template and same `raise_exception` mechanism, but a different trigger (consecutive same-role messages) and a broader ask (a switch to override template exceptions). This report is narrower and does not need that switch: the id llama-server rejects is the id **llama-server just returned**, so it can be reconciled server-side without overriding the template's check at all. Noting also that #11402 was closed by the stale bot rather than fixed, and drew a "still broken" report in June 2026 — so this failure class appears to be live.

### Steps to Reproduce

**Step 1 — ask for a tool call and note the returned `id`:**

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"List files in /tmp using the tool."}],
  "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"list_directory","description":"List",
    "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"}}}}}],
  "temperature":0,"max_tokens":50}'
```

Returns `"id": "1697377797897"` (stable across runs at `temperature 0`).

**Step 2 — echo that exact `id` back as a tool result, per the API contract:**

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "messages":[
    {"role":"user","content":"List files in /tmp using the tool."},
    {"role":"assistant","tool_calls":[{"id":"1697377797897","type":"function",
      "function":{"name":"list_directory","arguments":"{\"path\":\"/tmp\"}"}}]},
    {"role":"tool","tool_call_id":"1697377797897","content":"a.txt"}],
  "tools":[{"type":"function","function":{"name":"list_directory","description":"List",
    "parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"path":{"type":"string"}}}}}],
  "temperature":0,"max_tokens":30}'
```

**Expected:** a normal completion.
**Actual:** HTTP 400.

**Control — the identical request with a 9-character alphanumeric id succeeds:**

```bash
# same as Step 2 but with "id"/"tool_call_id" = "abc123def"
{"choices":[{"finish_reason":"stop","message":{"role":"assistant",
  "content":"It is currently 18°C in Geneva."}}], ...}
```

One field apart: `1697377797897` → 400, `abc123def` → 200. Also observed non-conforming across sampled runs: `1`, `5321`, `2561782006`, `vJIdfyOPVLTiPdEcK5w1lpHWALostelO` (32), `f4403c38-0c02-4362-a497-d804a2000d47` (36, with hyphens).

Requests *without* tool history are unaffected — a plain prompt, and a first turn that carries `tools`, both return 200.

Not bisected.

Automatic parser generation failed:
------------
While executing CallExpression at line 62, column 36 in source:
...9 %}↵                {{- raise_exception(\"Tool call IDs should be alphanumeric s...
                                           ^
Error: Jinja Exception: Tool call IDs should be alphanumeric strings with length 9!",

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

When using a thinking model (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B) as a backend for **GitHub Copilot Chat in Agent mode** (VS Code), the server returns a 500 error `Failed to parse input at pos N` during multi-turn agentic tool-calling workflows.

1. Copilot sends a chat completion request with many tools (`read_file`, `grep_search`, `semantic_search`, `list_dir`, `memory`, etc.)
2. The model thinks inside `<think>...</think>`, then calls a tool via `<tool_call>...</tool_call>`
3. The tool result is returned to the model, which thinks again and calls more tools
4. This multi-step loop continues until the model produces a final answer

During these multi-turn interactions, the model frequently outputs a short natural language transition sentence between `</think>` and `<tool_call>`, such as:
- `让我再查看一些额外的信息来完善分析。` ("Let me check some more information to refine the analysis.")

With a Qwen3-family chat template (Qwen3.5/3.6 MoE, embedded GGUF template, handled by the auto-parser path) and `chat_template_kwargs: {"enable_thinking": false}`, the `tool_choice: "required"` constraint (and likewise a named function `tool_choice`) is **not enforced**: the model free-runs plain prose until `max_tokens` (`finish_reason: "length"`), returns no `tool_calls`, and `content` stays empty when the run ends inside what the parser treats as reasoning.

The rest of the turn — usually a perfectly good `analysis` block and a valid tool call — is discarded.

items.title: Eval bug: Speculative decoding (draft-mtp / draft-dspark): greedy output diverges from vanilla on quantized targets
items.body:
## Summary

Under greedy sampling (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`), **draft-model** speculative decoding can produce different text than a non-speculative run when the **target is quantized** (e.g. Q4_K_M). The same setups match on a **bf16 target**. **Ngram** speculation on the same quantized target stays lossless even when drafts are accepted.

This contradicts the expected property that speculative decoding is lossless for greedy decode (draft proposes; target verifies).

Related: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/25173 (`draft-dspark`), but the issue is **not DSpark-only**.

## Environment (local repro)

- Hardware: AMD Strix Halo iGPU
- Backend: Vulkan (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`)
- Branch: PR #25173
- Others have also reported similar mismatches on **CUDA** (not re-run here)

## Expected

Greedy speculative output == greedy vanilla output for the same target weights / seed / prompt.

## Actual / evidence

Probe prompt (thinking off):

> What happens when a browser requests https://example.com? Five bullet points.

### Matrix (Vulkan)

| Setup | Spec active? | Match vanilla? |
|-------|----------------|----------------|
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, vanilla ×2 | n/a | **OK** (deterministic) |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-simple` (drafted, 0 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `ngram-mod` (4/8 accepted) | yes | **OK** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 | yes (e.g. 80/336) | **BUG** |
| Qwen3-8B **Q4_K_M**, `draft-dspark`, `-fa off` | yes | **BUG** (still) |
| Qwen3-8B **bf16**, `draft-dspark` n_max=7 (4 prompts) | yes | **OK** (4/4) |
| Gemma-4-12B Q4 + `draft-mtp` n_max=4 | yes (169/340) | **BUG** |

Example Q4 DSpark fork (both `finish=stop`):

- vanilla: `...checks if it has a cached copy of the website's SSL/TLS certificate...`
- dspark: `...checks if the system has a valid certificate for **example.com**...`

## What this is / is not

- **Is quantization-related:** yes (Q4 breaks; bf16 OK for DSpark).
- **Is not “all speculative”:** ngram paths match on the same Q4 target, including with accepts.
- **Is not DSpark/DFlash-only:** Gemma **MTP** also diverges on Q4.
- **Is not Qwen-only:** Gemma-4 + MTP also fails.
- **Is not vanilla Q4 nondeterminism:** two vanilla Q4 runs match.
- **Is not FA-only:** DSpark still mismatches with `-fa off`.
- **Target weights likely fine:** ngram uses the same greedy accept/verify sampler path (`common_sampler_sample_and_accept_n` in server) and stays lossless → points to **draft-model speculative paths** (MTP / DSpark: draft ctx, KV, embd/injection, multi-token target batching) interacting badly with **quantized** target compute—not permanent weight corruption.
- **Type-cast root cause:** not isolated; path-dependent Q4 numerics remain a plausible contributor.

## Root cause (AI slop analysis, may be bs)

For Qwen3-Coder-style templates (common_chat_params_init_qwen3_coder, common/chat.cpp),
one trigger pattern is added per tool:

- common/chat.cpp:1218 - tool_call_starts = { "< tool_call>" } plus
  "<function=" + name + ">" for every tool (264 patterns for 263 tools)
- common/chat.cpp:1325 - each becomes a COMMON_GRAMMAR_TRIGGER_TYPE_WORD trigger
- common/sampling.cpp:227 - each word is escaped into its own regex pattern
- src/llama-grammar.cpp:1291 - each pattern compiled to its own std::regex

While awaiting the trigger, every accepted token runs through
llama_grammar_accept_impl (src/llama-grammar.cpp:1401):

    grammar.trigger_buffer += piece;   // grows without bound
    for (const auto & trigger_pattern : grammar.trigger_patterns) {
        auto start = trigger_pattern.find(grammar.trigger_buffer);

find() (src/llama-grammar.cpp:377) is a full std::regex_search over the entire
accumulated output, once per pattern, per token. Total work is O(n_tools x
n_tokens^2) character scans with libstdc++ regex.

## Measured cost

Standalone benchmark replicating that loop (264 literal patterns like
`<\ function\=tool_i>`, 1978 tokens at ~3.8 chars/token to match the request
above), g++ -O2, Ryzen 9 9950X3D:

    patterns=10   -> 0.30 ms/token
    patterns=50   -> 1.50 ms/token
    patterns=100  -> 3.02 ms/token
    patterns=264  -> 8.00 ms/token

Linear in tool count. ~8 ms/token added to the decode step accounts for the
observed 47 -> 30 tok/s drop, and it grows with output length since the buffer is
never trimmed.

Minimal repro (core loop only):

    #include <regex>
    #include <string>
    #include <vector>
    #include <chrono>
    #include <cstdio>

    int main() {
        const int n_patterns = 264, n_tokens = 1978;
        std::vector<std::regex> re;
        for (int i = 0; i < n_patterns; i++)
            re.emplace_back("<\\function\\=tool_" + std::to_string(i) + "\\>");
        std::string buf;
        auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
        for (int t = 0; t < n_tokens; t++) {
            buf += "abc ";
            for (const auto & r : re) {
                std::smatch m;
                std::regex_search(buf, m, r); // find() over the whole buffer
            }
        }
        double ms = std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(
            std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0).count();
        printf("%.2f ms/token\n", ms / n_tokens);
    }

Secondary effect: the grammar (PEG parser over all tool schemas -> GBNF -> parse +
regex compilation) is rebuilt on every request (tools/server/server-common.cpp:1326,
tools/server/server-context.cpp:1690), which adds ~0.3-2 s to TTFT in my runs.

## Suggested fixes

1. Trim trigger_buffer to the last max_pattern_len - 1 chars when all patterns are
   literals (a literal match cannot start earlier than that). Per-token cost drops
   from O(buffer) to O(max_len). Fall back to the full buffer for arbitrary regex
   patterns.
2. Or merge the word triggers into one alternation pattern
   (<\ function\=(name1|name2|...)>) - one search instead of N.
3. Or use std::string::find (memchr-based) instead of std::regex for literal
   patterns.
4. Cache the compiled grammar across requests keyed by (template, tools,
   tool_choice) to avoid the per-request rebuild.

items.title: Misc. bug: Agent mode, shelling command executing can fail caused by whitespace in path
items.body:
### Name and Version

llama-b9553-bin-win-cuda-12.4-x64 version
On win11
When I asked agent to execute git commands in a path containing "unreal engine", it gives me error




### Operating systems

Windows

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```shell

```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

### 1. Symptom Log
During this task, the shell execution failure evolved through three distinct stages:

Stage I: Command Parsing Error — When attempting to use compound commands (e.g., `&&`, `|`), the system returned an error stating the command "is not recognized as an internal or external command."

Stage II: Path Truncation Error — When processing paths containing spaces (e.g., `Unreal Projects`), Git reported: `fatal: cannot change to '"D:\Unreal': Invalid argument`.

Stage III: Environment Isolation/Permission Error — Attempts to switch drives (e.g., `d:`) or execute `dir /x` resulted in "Tool execution was denied" or path resolution exceptions.


### 2. Root Cause Analysis
A. The "Double-Escaping Trap" in the Wrapper Layer
This is the core issue. The Agent does not send your instructions directly to the Windows Shell; instead, it encapsulates them via an intermediate layer (Wrapper).

Logic Chain: User Input → Agent Logic → Wrapper Encapsulation → OS Shell.

Point of Failure: When `&&` or `"` is used in a command, the Wrapper layer automatically wraps the command in an extra set of quotes to "protect" it. Consequently, the instruction received by the OS becomes something like `'\"command1 && command2\"'`.

Result: The Windows OS interprets the entire string (including the quotes and `&&`) as a single filename rather than a sequence of commands. Since no file exists with a name like `"cd & echo..."`, the system throws the "is not recognized" error.

B. Space-Delimiter Conflict

Logic Chain: Windows path contains spaces → Git requires quotes around the path → Wrapper adds yet another layer of quotes.

Point of Failure: The string ultimately passed to Git becomes `'"D:\Unreal Projects\..."'`. During parsing, due to lost escape characters or positional shifts, Git's parser treats the path as terminated upon encountering the first space, resulting in an "Invalid argument" error.

C. Non-Persistent Process Context

Point of Failure: In many Agent implementations, every call to `exec_shell_command` effectively launches a brand-new, independent process.

Result: Executing `d:` in Process A successfully switches the drive, but Process A terminates immediately after execution completes. The next command executes within Process B, still defaulting to the `C:\` drive. Consequently, `cd` and drive-switching operations are logically "ineffective."

### Summary

With `DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731` (GGUF) served by `llama-server` with `--jinja` and tools armed, generation **terminated mid-tag with `finish_reason: "stop"`** on three consecutive agent turns — each time exactly at the point where the reasoning stream contained literal DSML closing fragments (`</｜DSML｜parameter>`, `</｜DSML｜invoke>`). The final streamed token was `tool_c` — an *incomplete* `</｜DSML｜tool_calls>` closing tag. The client-visible result is an agent that appears to stop mid-tool-call, and (because the truncated message is persisted into history) a self-perpetuating loop: each follow-up turn imitates the truncated pattern and gets cut at the same place.

### Environment

- `llama-server` build 10573, commit `d775b8967` (master, 2026-08-22), AppleClang 21, Darwin arm64
- Backends: Metal (M5 Max) + one RPC worker (DGX Spark GB10), `--split-mode layer`
- Model: `unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF` UD-Q8_K_XL (5 shards) + `dspark-DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-Q8_0.gguf` draft
- Flags: `--spec-type draft-dspark --spec-draft-n-max 3 -c 393216 --flash-attn on --cache-type-k f16 --cache-type-v f16 --jinja --temp 0.6 --top-p 0.95`
- Effective slot state observed: `chat_format: "peg-native"`, `reasoning_format: "deepseek"`, `generation_prompt: "<｜Assistant｜><think>"`

### Observed (3 consecutive turns, harness session transcript)

| Turn | input tokens | output tokens | finish | stream ends at |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~165,000 | ~120 (est.) | stop | reasoning text `...a1b2c3d` + `</｜DSML｜parameter>` |
| 2 | 168,991 | 126 | stop | `...a1b2c3` + `</｜DSML｜parameter>\n</｜DSML｜invoke>\n</｜DSML｜tool_c` |
| 3 | 169,132 | 119 | stop | same fragment, same cut point |

Final reasoning deltas for turn 3 (verbatim, from the client event log):

```
... 'c', '3', '</｜DSML｜', 'parameter', '>', '\n', '</｜DSML｜', 'inv', 'oke', '>', '\n', '</｜DSML｜', 'tool', '_c'
```

The model was composing a file-edit tool call whose parameter value contained backtick-quoted hex strings (`` `a1b2c3d4e5f6` ``). The reasoning text shows the model interleaving protocol markup into the thinking channel; the stream then terminates *mid-tag*. No EOS content token is visible in the client stream — the stop appears to come from the serving side's handling of the DSML structure, not from a deliberate EOS the model wrote.

### Expected

Reasoning/thinking content should be treated as opaque text: a stray or partial DSML closing tag inside reasoning must not end generation. If the model truly opens a tool call, the parser should wait for a well-formed close; a malformed close should yield a parse error or plain text — never a silent mid-tag `stop`.

### Minimal repro attempt (negative result at short context)

A direct request asking the model to quote `</｜DSML｜parameter>` inside its reasoning, with a dummy tool armed, completed normally at short context (`finish: stop`, 271 completion tokens, tag quoted intact). So the failure is **not** triggered by the tag alone — the incidents happened at **~165–169K context depth** in an agentic multi-tool flow (the harness session had ~100 prior tool calls). Possibly depth-dependent (parser state / attention degradation at depth making the model emit protocol markup mid-reasoning more likely, and/or the parser's early-stop engaging once it does).

### Why it matters

The truncated message is persisted by clients as a normal completed turn (`finish: stop`), and the model then imitates its own truncated pattern on the next turn — the failure is self-reinforcing within a session. Three identical stops in a row required abandoning the session.

### Related

- vllm-project/vllm#48931 — DSML parser fragility when the model omits the `<｜DSML｜tool_calls>` START wrapper (V4, long context)
- ggml-org/llama.cpp#25618 — draft-dspark/draft-mtp greedy divergence on quantized targets
- ggml-org/llama.cpp#26554 — DSpark + V4-Flash long-generation abort

Happy to provide the full client event log (JSONL), server logs, or test patches.

built with GNU 16.1.1 for Linux x86_64

### Operating systems

Linux

### GGML backends

HIP

### Hardware

AMD Strix Halo (Ryzen AI Max+ 395)

### Models

Ling-3.0-flash-Q5_K_M from https://huggingface.co/bloomer010/Ling-3.0-flash-GGUF

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

In a multi-turn tool using chat, the model sometimes emits `<tool_call>...</tool_call>` from inside its reasoning channel and stops without ever closing `</think>`. The whole turn is then swallowed into reasoning_content.

Root cause
Bailing V3 has no specialized parser in common/chat.cpp, so it falls through to the generic autoparser, which sets a single reasoning terminator (`thinking_end_tags = {"</think>"}`) with no <tool_call> fallback. When the model opens a tool call before closing `</think>`, nothing terminates reasoning and the output is mis-routed.

Behaviour like this is already handled for some other models (these thinking+tool models add tool call openers as reasoning terminators).

For example:
Qwen3-Coder: `thinking_end_tags = {"</think>", "<tool_call>"}`
DeepSeek V3.2: `thinking_end_tags = {THINK_END, FC_START}`
Kimi K2 (common_chat_params_init_kimi_k2) handles this exact behavior, with the maintainer comment: "this model is CRAZY … it can call tools at the end of reasoning without closing reasoning", and adds `<|tool_calls_section_begin|> / <|tool_call_begin|>` as terminators.
Bailing V3's Kimi-K2-like tendency to call tools mid-reasoning isn't covered by the generic autoparser.

Suggested fix
Add <tool_call> to Bailing V3's reasoning terminators (similar to Kimi K2/Qwen3-Coder fixes)

items.title: Eval bug: gemma4 peg template intermittently unparseable with long multi-line tool-call string arguments
items.body:
## Summary

Native tool calling with the `peg-gemma4` chat template intermittently
produces unparseable output when a tool call must carry long multi-line
string arguments (source code with quotes, newlines, and digest strings).
Short-argument calls (single paths, small queries) are reliable in the same
sessions. Failures surface server-side as
`common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-gemma4 output: …` followed by an
unusable response body.

## Environment

- llama.cpp builds `14d3ba4` and `b10078` (both reproduce)
- Model: Gemma 4 26B-A4B instruction-tuned, QAT, UD-Q4_K_XL GGUF
- macOS / Metal, `--jinja`, native tool calling, `--parallel 1`
- Speculative decoding via `--spec-type draft-mtp` (an MTP draft head);
  failures also reproduce with speculation disabled
- Sampling: temp 0.2, top-k 64, top-p 0.95, repeat-penalty 1.0

## Observations

1. Repro: seed a workspace with a small `calc.py` + `test_calc.py`; request
   an edit that requires sending replacement file content as a tool-call
   string argument. First read-only calls parse fine; the edit call fails
   intermittently (most attempts in our runs).
2. Failure content shows two modes: (a) degenerate repetition of tool-call
   blocks or of a short token sequence, accelerated to ~99% draft
   acceptance by MTP; (b) malformed special-token quoting inside the
   argument payload (`<|"|>`-delimited strings interrupted by content).
3. Raising repetition penalties makes things worse: penalized sampling
   corrupted a verbatim tool name by one character in our logs
   (`…_3c6d768552ba` → `…_3d6d768552ba`), so format fidelity requires
   penalty-free sampling.
4. Enabling native thinking (`--reasoning-budget`) increases failure
   frequency; disabling it does not eliminate failures.

## Ask

- Whether the peg-gemma4 grammar can constrain string interiors (or recover
  from stray bytes) rather than rejecting the entire generation.
- Whether draft acceptance should be dampened when the accepted window is
  self-similar (anti-loop guard under speculative decoding).

Happy to provide full event-log excerpts and server-log signatures on request.

items.title: gpt-oss/harmony: non-streaming final without channel markup hard-throws 500 ("does not match the expected peg-native format") — lenient fallback unreachable
items.body:
### Name and Version

```
version: 1 (8086439)
built with GNU 15.2.0 for Linux x86_64
```

Also verified present on current `master` (`a4107133a634`, 2026-07-04) — see "First Bad Commit / still-present" below.

### Operating systems

Linux (x86_64)

### Which llama.cpp modules do you know to be affected?

llama-server

### Command line

```
llama-server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8091 \
  -m gpt-oss-120b-mxfp4-00001-of-00003.gguf \
  -ngl 99 -ub 512 -c 32768 --jinja -fa on
```

### Problem description & steps to reproduce

For `gpt-oss` (harmony format), a **non-streaming** chat completion whose final message contains bare content with **no channel markup** hard-throws HTTP 500 instead of returning the content.

**Root-cause chain (all still present on current master):**

1. `common_chat_params_init_gpt_oss()` in `common/chat.cpp` builds a PEG grammar whose top-level alternation (`final_msg | unsolicited`, or `tool_call | final_msg` with tools) requires `<|channel|>...<|message|>` markup on every branch. There is no content-only / bare-final fallback arm.
2. When the model emits a content-only final (which gpt-oss does intermittently — notably under a system prompt demanding "strict JSON only, no channels, no reasoning"), the final parse fails.
3. For the **non-streaming** path, `tools/server/server-task.h:388` calls `update_chat_msg(content, /*is_partial=*/false, ...)`.
4. The lenient partial-AST fallback in `common/chat.cpp` (`if (is_partial && result.end > 0) { ... return msg; }`) is therefore unreachable, and the mismatch throws `"The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format"`, surfaced to the client as a bare HTTP 500.

No CLI flag relaxes this for gpt-oss (`--jinja` cannot be dropped for this model). Streaming requests are unaffected because they exercise the `is_partial=true` path.

**Repro:** `POST 127.0.0.1:8091/v1/chat/completions`, model `gpt-oss-120b`, with a system prompt insisting the assistant reply with strict JSON and nothing else — no reasoning, no channel markup:

```json
{
  "model": "gpt-oss-120b",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a strict JSON API. Reply with a single JSON object and NOTHING else — no reasoning, no channel markup, no prose."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Return {\"ok\": true}"}
  ]
}
```

- Reproduces the 500 **5/5** with the strict-JSON system prompt above.
- A plain "reply with JSON" (no strict-no-channel instruction) returns 200.
- **Non-deterministic** on identical requests — hit rate ~23% across mixed structured/JSON traffic in production.

**First Bad Commit / still-present:** Not a regression — this is a design limitation of the harmony non-streaming path. Verified byte-identical on build `8086439` (2026-06-17) and current `master` `a4107133a634` (2026-07-04): the `common_chat_params_init_gpt_oss` grammar, the `is_partial`-gated fallback, and `server-task.h:388`'s hardcoded `is_partial=false` are unchanged across the ~190 commits between them.

**Suggested directions (non-prescriptive):**

- Allow a content-only final to parse leniently (treat unmarked trailing content as the `final` channel) rather than hard-throwing; **or**
- On the non-streaming final path, fall back to the lenient (`is_partial`-style) parse before throwing, so a well-formed-but-unmarked final degrades to plain content instead of a 500.

Related-but-distinct precedent: the Gemma-4 analog (#25072 / PR #25100, closed without merge) was ruled a template bug; this one is specifically the gpt-oss non-streaming final path.

### Relevant log output

```
srv  ... : ... "The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format"
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
```

## Summary

With `response_format: {"type":"json_schema", ...}` on a model running under `Chat format: peg-native`, **roughly 35–40% of requests fail with HTTP 500**:

```
The model produced output that does not match the expected peg-native format
```

The parse failure is a **consequence, not the cause**. Streaming the same request shows the generation itself ends mid-JSON-object: `finish_reason` is absent and the content is a truncated object, well under `max_tokens`. Non-streaming then hits `common_chat_peg_parse` (`common/chat.cpp:2683`) and throws.

Without `response_format` the same prompt succeeds 6/6 and `reasoning_content` is extracted correctly every time. The grammar is what turns it on.

## Version / environment

| | |
|---|---|
| llama.cpp | `b9739` / `8452824611be321246f33339727f60a90c02c277` |
| build | CUDA, GNU 13.3.0, Linux x86_64 |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS |
| GPU | 2× RTX 5060 Ti / 4060 Ti, driver 610.43.02 |
| chat format | `peg-native` (reported in the log; see the note under §2) |

```
llama-server \
  --model Ornith-1.0-35B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080 \
  --n-gpu-layers 99 \
  --ctx-size 262144 \
  --flash-attn on
```

No `--reasoning-format`, no `--jinja` flag (jinja is on by default in this build).

## Reproduction

Any prompt that makes the model think for a while and then emit a JSON object. Request body:

```json
{
  "model": "ornith-35b",
  "max_tokens": 8000,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "<extraction prompt over ~400 tokens of text>"}],
  "response_format": {
    "type": "json_schema",
    "json_schema": {
      "name": "m",
      "strict": true,
      "schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "additionalProperties": false,
        "required": ["mentions"],
        "properties": {
          "mentions": {
            "type": "array",
            "items": {
              "type": "object",
              "additionalProperties": false,
              "required": ["brand","company","product","stance","rank","reason","source_urls"],
              "properties": {
                "brand":   {"type": "string"},
                "company": {"type": "string"},
                "product": {"type": "string"},
                "stance":  {"type": "string", "enum": ["positive","negative","neutral"]},
                "rank":    {"type": "integer"},
                "reason":  {"type": "string"},
                "source_urls": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}}
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

No `$ref`, no deep nesting. Sent straight to `llama-server`, sequentially, one at a time.

**Measured, 26 requests total:**

| condition | result |
|---|---|
| with `json_schema` | **7/20 → HTTP 500** (35%) |
| **without** `json_schema`, same prompt | **6/6 OK**, `reasoning_content` 1728–5349 chars every time |
| with `json_schema`, English-only prompt and output | **5/8 → HTTP 500** (62%) — not an encoding issue |

## Evidence

### 1. The generation stops early — it is not only a parsing problem

`common/chat.cpp:2663` returns partial results instead of throwing when `is_partial`, so the same request with `"stream": true` shows what the non-streaming path hides:

```
ok:     finish_reason=stop   content=1486 chars   → complete JSON
failed: finish_reason=None   content=370 chars    → JSON truncated mid-object
```

Server log for a failing request:

```
slot release: id 2 | task 296833 | stop processing: n_tokens = 1914, truncated = 0
```

~1449 decoded tokens against `max_tokens: 8000`. The model emitted a stop token in the middle of a JSON object that the grammar should still have been constraining.

### 2. What the parser choked on

`common/chat.cpp:2681` logs the unparsed remainder at WARN, so this needs no debug build:

```
W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: {
  "mentions": [
    {
      "brand": "FlowAccount",
      "company": "..."
        ,
    "product": "FlowAccount"
```

and sometimes:

```
W common_chat_peg_parse: unparsed peg-native output: ```json
{
  "mentions": [
```

Two things to note:

- the unparsed remainder is **the entire content from its first character** — the parser consumed the reasoning section and then matched nothing of the content
- the model sometimes emits a **markdown fence** before the JSON, which a schema-derived grammar alone would not permit

The first of those is, I think, explained rather than mysterious. `common_chat_peg_parse` parses `generation_prompt + input`:

```cpp
const std::string effective_input = params.generation_prompt.empty()
    ? input
    : params.generation_prompt + input;
```

so the prefilled `<think>` from the template (§4) is present and the reasoning section matches. If the content rule is a PEG *sequence* ending in a terminator such as `<|im_end|>`, then a truncated generation makes the whole sequence fail without consuming anything, and `result.end` stays at the point where content began — which is exactly what the log shows. In other words **the parse failure is fully accounted for by §1; the open question is why generation stops.**

A note on the format name: `COMMON_CHAT_FORMAT_PEG_NATIVE` is set in several places — the differential autoparser (`common/chat-auto-parser-generator.cpp:48`) and a number of specialized template paths (`common/chat.cpp:972`, `1092`, `1386`) — so `Chat format: peg-native` in the log does not by itself say which parser was built. `using differential autoparser` is only logged at debug level, and I have not restarted this server with `--verbose` yet. Happy to, if it helps.

### 3. If this is the autoparser path, the grammar is not lazy

`common/chat-auto-parser-generator.cpp:87`

```cpp
data.grammar_lazy = !has_response_format && inputs.tool_choice == COMMON_CHAT_TOOL_CHOICE_AUTO;
```

`has_response_format` is true, so `grammar_lazy == false` — the grammar is meant to be constraining from the first token.

### 4. `<think>` is prefilled by the template, so the model's output starts *inside* the thinking block

The generation prompt ends with:

```jinja
{%- if add_generation_prompt %}
    {{- '<|im_start|>assistant\n' }}
    {%- if enable_thinking is defined and enable_thinking is false %}
        {{- '<think>\n\n</think>\n\n' }}
    {%- else %}
        {{- '<think>\n' }}
    {%- endif %}
{%- endif %}
```

The opening `<think>` is in the prompt, not in the sampled output; the model must emit the closing `</think>` itself. I suspect the interaction between a grammar built from the whole template structure and a sampled sequence that begins already inside one of that structure's blocks, but I have not verified this — it is where I would look first.

### 5. `--reasoning-format` is not the lever

Restarted with `LLAMA_ARG_THINK=deepseek` and re-measured: **8/20 failures (40%)**, indistinguishable from the 35% baseline at this sample size, and the log still reports `Chat format: peg-native` with `unparsed` warnings unchanged. Setting `reasoning_format` per request in the body has no effect either (2/8 failures).

## Ruled out (so you don't have to)

- **Not a gateway/proxy artefact** — reproduced by `curl` straight at `llama-server`; a logging proxy confirmed the body forwarded by our gateway is byte-identical to the client's.
- **Not UTF-8 / non-Latin text** — an English-only prompt and output fails *more* often (62%).
- **Not `max_tokens`** — generation stops at ~1449 of 8000.
- **Not lazy grammar** — see §3.
- **Not `--reasoning-format`** — see §5.

## Secondary observation

For a failing request in streaming mode the client receives HTTP 200 with a **truncated JSON body and no `finish_reason`**, rather than an error. The partial-parse branch is doing what it was written to do, but from the client's side an incomplete structured answer is indistinguishable from a complete one until parsing fails downstream. It may be worth marking that case explicitly.

## Reproducibility caveat

The model is a custom fine-tune (`Ornith-1.0-35B`) that I cannot share, and I have not reproduced this on a public model — the two public reasoning models on this box are 27B/32B and the GPUs are occupied, so a CPU run was not practical for a 20-request measurement. The template is ChatML-shaped with `<tool_call>`/`<function>` blocks and the prefilled `<think>` shown in §4, and I can paste it in full if that is useful.

I am happy to run a patch, a debug build, or `--verbose` against this exact workload and report back — the failure reproduces within a handful of requests, so the turnaround is minutes.

items.title: Qwen3-Coder parser: lazy tool-call trigger never fires when model skips both <tool_call> and <function=
items.body:
## Summary

The Qwen3-Coder chat parser (`common_chat_params_init_qwen3_coder`, added in #26252) has a documented workaround for models that omit the opening `<tool_call>` wrapper while still emitting `<function=name>`. In practice the model can deviate further than that, abandoning the structured format entirely, and the lazy grammar trigger never fires, so the response falls through as plain content instead of `tool_calls`.

## Root cause

The trigger that switches into constrained decoding only watches for a literal `<tool_call>` or `<function=` substring in the raw output stream:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/f5919bf458ef190468b5c329bb293f8a54a1e69c/common/chat.cpp#L1241

```cpp
(reasoning << p.content(p.until_one_of({ "<tool_call>", "<function=" })) << tool_calls);
```

The existing workaround, one line above, acknowledges partial omission:

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/f5919bf458ef190468b5c329bb293f8a54a1e69c/common/chat.cpp#L1232

```cpp
// Qwen3-Coder models may occasionally omit the <tool_call> token.
```

...and makes the *first* call's `<tool_call>\n` wrapper optional in the grammar. That only helps if the model still emits `<function=`. When it emits neither trigger string at all, `p.content()` consumes the whole response as free text and the tool-call branch is never entered.

Auto-detection for this parser (matched by the chat template containing `<tool_call>`, `<function=`, `<parameter=`):

https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/f5919bf458ef190468b5c329bb293f8a54a1e69c/common/chat.cpp#L3182-L3186

## Repro

- Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Q8_0
- Build: a local rebase/merge commit (b10361) on top of #26252 (f5919bf458ef190468b5c329bb293f8a54a1e69c, merged 2026-08-02, that commit is linked above for the source references since the local merge commit itself was never pushed and has no public ref; confirmed the referenced lines are unchanged between the two, this is not a missing-fix situation, the specialized parser is active)
- Chat template: Jinja template instructing `<tool_call>\n<function=name>\n<parameter=...>` (matches the auto-detect heuristic above)
- `tool_choice`: unset/auto, any temperature
- Real production output, verbatim, no `tool_calls` in the response, `finish_reason: stop`:

```
I'll check your cron jobs to find the daily briefing one and trigger it.

[cron(action='list')]
```

The model had a real tool available (name `cronjob`, note it also got the name wrong) but never entered tool-call grammar at all; the response was delivered as ordinary assistant text.

## Why this isn't just a bad prompt

Confirmed deterministic and prompt-dependent, not sampling noise: replaying the exact same request at `temperature=0` reproduces this exact fabricated output 5/5 times, byte-for-byte identical. The same request at default temperature produces a correct `tool_calls` response 5/5 times. Same template, same tool schema, same model, only the sampled decoding path differs, and greedy decoding happens to land on a path that never emits either trigger string for this particular prompt.

## Suggested direction

Broaden the "did the model intend a tool call" signal beyond exact-match on `<tool_call>`/`<function=`, e.g. a lower-confidence secondary trigger on tool-name-shaped call syntax in free text, or, if that's out of scope, a docs note that the existing omission workaround doesn't cover the model abandoning the format entirely would at least set expectations correctly.
